hook: Two men in here hadn't touched the ground in 355 days.
narration: Two of the men inside had not touched the ground in three hundred fifty-five days.
Before leaving, NASA astronaut Mark Vande Hei and cosmonaut Pyotr Dubrov said goodbye to the crew staying behind.
On March thirtieth, their Soyuz backed away from the space station, with commander Anton Shkaplerov flying it by hand.
Only the center section, called the descent module, returns to Earth.
Hours later it was falling over Kazakhstan under a single striped parachute.
Russian helicopters circled the landing zone as it came down.
[short pause] Touchdown came at five twenty-eight in the evening, in a burst of dust.
Recovery crews pulled the commander out first, to open a path to the other two.
outcome: All three were lifted out, and Vande Hei came home with the U.S. record for the longest single spaceflight.
title: 355 days in space, then this landing
description:
NASA astronaut Mark Vande Hei and cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov and Anton Shkaplerov landed in the Soyuz MS-19 near Dzhezkazgan, Kazakhstan, on March 30, 2022, ending a 355-day mission for Vande Hei and Dubrov.
